record.paper_title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds
record.context_brief: Hopf conjecture on Euler characteristic and curvature
record.original_question: If M is an aspherical closed manifold of even dimension, must its Euler characteristic satisfy (-1)^(dim(M)/2) * χ(M) >= 0? More generally, if M is a closed Riemannian manifold of even dimension, must one have (-1)^(dim(M)/2) * χ(M) > 0 when sec(M) < 0, (-1)^(dim(M)/2) * χ(M) >= 0 when sec(M) <= 0, χ(M) >= 0 when sec(M) >= 0, and χ(M) > 0 when sec(M) > 0?

artifact.category_tag: Hopf conjecture on Euler characteristic and curvature
artifact.status_search_result: The Hopf conjectures on the sign of the Euler characteristic for even-dimensional closed manifolds of definite sectional curvature, and their aspherical analogue (the Singer–Hopf conjecture), remain open in general. They hold trivially for surfaces (Gauss–Bonnet) and in dimension 4 (Chern–Gauss–Bonnet plus Poincaré duality), and partial results are known in special settings (e.g. Kähler hyperbolic manifolds by Gromov), but the cases of dimension ≥ 6 are unresolved.
